questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Probability of a Complement
questions.problem: Given that $P(A)=0.5,$ $P(A\cap B)=0.4,$ and $P(A\cup B)=0.8,$ find $P({B}^{′}).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $P(B)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ 0.8 & =0.5+P(B)-0.4 \\ P(B) & =0.8+0.4-0.5 \\ P(B) & =0.7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P({B}^{′}) & =1-P(B) \\  & =1-0.7 \\  & =0.3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Probability of a Union
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $P(A\cap B)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ \frac{7}{10} & =\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2}{5}-P(A\cap B) \\ P(A\cap B) & =\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2}{5}-\frac{7}{10} \\ P(A\cap B) & =\frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we construct the corresponding Venn diagram and shade the region $A\cup {B}^{′}.$

Finally, we have

$$
P(A\cup {B}^{′})=\frac{3}{10}+\frac{1}{5}+\frac{3}{10}=\frac{4}{5}.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Probability of a Complement
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $P(A)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ 0.75 & =P(A)+0.45-0.2 \\ P(A) & =0.75+0.2-0.45 \\  & =0.5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P({A}^{′}) & =1-P(A) \\  & =1-0.5 \\  & =0.5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Probability of a Complement
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $P(A)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ \frac{4}{5} & =P(A)+\frac{4}{15}-\frac{1}{15} \\ P(A) & =\frac{4}{5}+\frac{1}{15}-\frac{4}{15} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P({A}^{′}) & =1-P(A) \\  & =1-\frac{3}{5} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
